title: Engine ragdoll — pose-snapshot at spawn
notes: Closes the S132 visual-jump caveat: engine spawn-system currently positions bodies at root.position + template.body.anchor — a rest-pose layout that ignores where the meshes actually are at the moment of death. A bomber killed mid-stride teleports its limbs back to T-pose before the ragdoll starts integrating, producing a visible 1-frame jump.

Fix: project writes optional bodyPoses (Record<bodyName, {position[3], rotation?[3]}>) inside the RagdollSpawnRequest. The engine spawn-system uses each entry as the body's acquireBody position+rotation override; missing entries fall back to root+anchor as today (so existing callers stay backward-compatible).

Kaboom death-trigger composes bodyPoses from each mesh entity's LocalToWorld component (the render-cache writes world-space position+rotation+scale per Transform-bearing entity each frame). LocalToWorld is the natural source of truth — no parent-chain walk in the project, and the values match exactly what the renderer was about to draw.

Note: the engine spawn-system uses Rapier's acquireBody({ position, rotation? }) so engine-side support is already there. Rotation is Euler XYZ in radians (Rapier convention via the adapter's eulerToQuat). LocalToWorld stores rotation in degrees, so the kaboom trigger converts before writing bodyPoses.

stories.title: Extend ragdollSpawnRequest schema with optional bodyPoses
stories.summary: schemas/components/ragdoll.schema.json — ragdollSpawnRequest gains optional bodyPoses: { additionalProperties: { type: object, required: [position], properties: { position, rotation } } }. position is a 3-element number array (world-space, metres); rotation is an optional 3-element Euler-XYZ array (degrees to mirror Transform component convention; engine converts). Unknown body names + entries with malformed shape are silently ignored at the spawn-system level.
verification: acceptance: schemas/components/ragdoll.schema.json — ragdollSpawnRequest gains optional bodyPoses (Record<bodyName, {position[3], rotation?[3]}>). position required + 3 numbers; rotation optional + 3 numbers (degrees). additionalProperties:false on each entry; unknown body names ignored at spawn-system level.

stories.title: spawn-system honours bodyPoses when present (per-body anchor override)
stories.summary: engine/physics/ragdoll/spawn-system.ts — spawnRagdoll reads req.bodyPoses (passed alongside meshMap). For each body in template.bodies: if bodyPoses[body.name] exists, use {position, rotation} as the acquireBody pose; else fall back to the current origin+anchor + no rotation. The body entity's initial Transform component matches the spawn pose. Rotation passed to acquireBody is converted deg→rad here (engine convention is rad inside Rapier).
verification: acceptance: engine/physics/ragdoll/spawn-system.ts — spawnRagdoll reads req.bodyPoses. Per-body: if bodyPoses[name] exists with valid position, use as acquireBody pose (rotation converted deg→rad); else fall back to origin+anchor. Body entity's initial Transform mirrors the spawn pose (rotation in degrees on the Transform).

stories.title: Kaboom death-trigger composes bodyPoses from LocalToWorld before detach
stories.summary: examples/kaboom-crew/src/systems/death-trigger-system.ts — on the alive→false edge, BEFORE detaching Transform.parent on the 10 mesh entities, read each mesh's LocalToWorld { position, rotation, scale }. Build bodyPoses: Record<bodyName, { position, rotation }> from the read values (LTW rotation is already in radians; the schema declares degrees so the trigger writes deg). Skip bodies without an LTW (engine falls back to anchor). Include bodyPoses in the RagdollSpawnRequest alongside the existing meshMap + impulse + templateKey.
verification: acceptance: examples/kaboom-crew/src/systems/death-trigger-system.ts — death-trigger reads LocalToWorld on each mesh BEFORE detaching parent, builds bodyPoses (radian rotation converted to degrees). bodyPoses omitted from request when no mesh has LTW (clean backward-compat).

stories.title: Engine unit tests for bodyPoses override behaviour
stories.summary: tests/unit/ragdoll-bodyposes.test.ts — (1) spawn with bodyPoses positions bodies at the provided world coords (override template anchors); (2) partial bodyPoses: only some bodies overridden, the rest fall back to root+anchor; (3) bodyPoses[].rotation is honoured; (4) unknown body names in bodyPoses are silently skipped; (5) backward-compat — spawn without bodyPoses behaves exactly as before. Uses the real Rapier adapter to verify the body's world-space transform after one tick.
verification: acceptance: tests/unit/ragdoll-bodyposes.test.ts adds 5 tests — full override, partial override + anchor fallback, rotation honoured (deg→Rapier), unknown body names skipped, backward-compat no bodyPoses. All 5 pass with real Rapier adapter.

stories.title: Kaboom death-trigger writes bodyPoses from LocalToWorld
stories.summary: examples/kaboom-crew/tests/unit/death-trigger-system.test.ts — extend with: (1) mesh entities with LocalToWorld get their world position+rotation written into bodyPoses (10 entries, deg rotation); (2) mesh without LocalToWorld → no bodyPoses entry for that body (engine falls back to anchor); (3) bodyPoses passes through alongside meshMap when both are populated.
verification: acceptance: 4 new S133 tests in death-trigger-system.test.ts cover: 10 LTW entries → 10 bodyPoses, partial LTW only writes matching entries, radian→deg rotation conversion, empty LTW → no bodyPoses (omitted). All 12 trigger tests pass.
